- **Bulk-free reclamation**: Coalescing freed objects to reduce fragmentation and enable efficient reuse

questions.explanation:
## Why This Is Asked
Tests lock-free IPC, memory ordering, and cache-coherence handling on NUMA systems under contention.

## Key Concepts
- Lock-free ring buffers with per-slot sequence numbers to avoid ABA
- Memory ordering on x86-64, mfence usage, cache-line padding
- Backpressure handling and wrap-around semantics

## Code Example
```c
typedef struct { volatile uint64_t seq; uint8_t data[64]; char pad[56]; } Slot;
typedef struct { Slot slots[N]; _Atomic uint64_t head; _Atomic uint64_t tail; } Ring;
```

```c
// Push (producer)
uint64_t pos; do { pos = atomic_read(&ring->head); if (slot_full(pos)) continue; } while(!atomic_compare_exchange(&ring->head, pos, pos+1));
r ing->slots[pos & (N-1)].data = payload; ring->slots[pos & (N-1)].seq = pos; mfence();
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you extend to multi-consumer or multi-ported rings?
- What are the performance pitfalls and mitigations (false sharing, cache thrashing)?
